title: Customer Churn Analysis Report
executive_summary: This report analyzes a snapshot of 749 customers, revealing an overall churn rate of 37.7%. The most critical risk factors identified are monthly contracts, which show a 121% higher churn rate than annual contracts, and a specific at-risk segment with high support ticket volume and low satisfaction, exhibiting a 71% churn rate. Lifetime value scales significantly with plan tier, with Premium customers generating nearly four times the value of Basic customers.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 749 customers with an overall churn rate of 37.7% and an average monthly fee of $42.11.
Churn rates across plans are relatively consistent, ranging from 36.6% (Premium) to 38.9% (Basic). The Basic plan experiences the highest churn.
Churn rates by signup cohort show slight variation, with the 2024 cohort having the highest churn rate at 39.8% and the 2022 cohort the lowest at 36.7%.
Monthly contracts exhibit a churn rate of 48.3%, which is 121.1% higher than the 21.9% rate for Annual contracts.
An at-risk segment of 100 customers (defined as having 5+ support tickets and satisfaction score ≤ 2) shows a critical churn rate of 71.0%.
Customer tenure averages 20.8 months (median 19.0, std dev 13.2). The average satisfaction score is 3.42, with 27 records missing a score.
Lifetime value increases significantly with plan tier: Basic averages $463, Standard $869, and Premium $1,817. Premium LTV is 292.0% higher than Basic.

limitations: The analysis is based on a single snapshot and does not capture temporal trends or causality.
Satisfaction scores were missing for 27 customers, potentially biasing the average satisfaction metric.
Lifetime value calculations depend on the accuracy of the derived 'lifetime_value' column provided in the cleaned dataset.
conclusion: To reduce churn, immediate focus should be placed on converting monthly contract customers to annual plans and addressing the high-churn at-risk segment through targeted retention strategies. While Basic plans have slightly higher churn rates, the significantly higher LTV of Premium customers underscores the importance of retention efforts across all tiers.
